utility.notes: Xcel Energy's list of Colorado communities served (10/2015) shows Idaho Springs with gas and electricity service. The list names communities, not addresses, and the City's pages do not name the electric utility, so check the utility named on your electric bill before you apply for interconnection. Xcel says your customer account number and premise number are on your Xcel Energy billing statement.

value.name: Xcel Energy
value.notes: Applies only if Xcel Energy is the utility named on your electric bill. Xcel says all solar customers receive Net Energy Metering (NEM) benefits from a system installed on their premise.

county.notes: The City's 2026 fee schedule resolution is headed City of Idaho Springs, Clear Creek County, Colorado.

permit_authority.value: City of Idaho Springs (City Clerk's office, with SAFEbuilt building inspections)
permit_authority.notes: The permitting process begins locally at Idaho Springs City Hall, and the City Clerk's office is responsible for permitting. Under Sec. 21-7 of the Idaho Springs Municipal Code, no structure may be erected or altered until the City has issued a building permit. SAFEbuilt performs inspections in Idaho Springs, and the City sends questions about the building code to SAFEbuilt. The Clear Creek County Building Department regulates buildings within the unincorporated areas of Clear Creek County. The City's Building Department page does not give a way to check whether an address is inside city limits, so confirm this with City Hall before you apply.

permit_url.notes: The Building Department page links the Building Permit Application and says completed applications and forms may be submitted by email. The City Clerk's Permitting page also says completed permit applications can be submitted to the clerk by email. The City's handout lists solar energy as a plan review project and says plan review applications are submitted in person at 1711 Miner St, Idaho Springs. Ask City Hall which submission method applies to your solar application.

interconnection_url.notes: This Xcel Energy page applies only if Xcel Energy is your utility. Xcel says the solar application process is typically managed by your solar installer, with some help from you along the way. Xcel highly recommends that construction of your system not start until your application receives full approval from the Xcel Energy engineering team and all final agreements are fully signed. Xcel says the typical interconnection process can take up to 12 to 16 weeks after initial application submission if no additional grid upgrades are required. Xcel's process has the installer upload the final electrical inspection from the local municipality before Xcel's meter technician grants permission to operate (PTO). Xcel's permission to operate is separate from the City permit and the City's inspections.

battery_programs.notes: The City's Building Department page does not describe a battery or storage program. If Xcel Energy is your utility, Xcel runs its own battery program (Renewable Battery Connect).

required_documents.notes: The City's handout gives one submittal list for all plan review projects, including solar energy, and names no solar-specific documents. The City's pages do not list a solar Building Guide, so ask City Hall which Building Guide applies to a solar project. The City recommends an optional pre-application plan review if you are unsure about the building codes, process, or submittal requirements.

value: If Xcel Energy is your utility, have your installer start Xcel's solar application, because Xcel recommends that construction not start until the application is fully approved.
Request an optional pre-application plan review if you are unsure about the codes, process or submittal requirements.
Submit the building permit application to the City.
Pay the plan review fee set by City staff, which must be paid before review can start.
Planning and Zoning, the Building Department and the Fire Authority review the plans, and you submit plans to the Fire Chief.
Pay the remaining fees, because the permit is issued only after all departments approve the plans and all fees are paid.
Pick up the approved plans and inspection handout at City Hall, 1711 Miner St.
Schedule SAFEbuilt inspections, which are performed on Tuesdays and Thursdays, by calling (303) 450-8748.
Make sure the licensed contractor listed on the permit is present at related inspections.
If Xcel is your utility, your installer uploads the final electrical inspection from the local municipality to Xcel's application portal.

If Xcel is your utility, Xcel's meter technician then installs or reviews the meter and leaves a red door hanger granting permission to operate (PTO). Xcel says this means you are able to turn your system on.
inspection_steps.notes: The City's handout does not list which inspections a solar installation needs, so ask SAFEbuilt when you schedule. Xcel says a meter technician will attempt to install or review the metering within 20 business days of the meter request.

timeline_days.notes: The City's plan review handout says plan approval turnaround time varies.

value.program_or_pathway: Plan review building permit (solar energy is a listed plan review project)
other_conditions: All contractors who do work in Idaho Springs must be licensed in Idaho Springs.
All residential construction must have a building permit and a city licensed contractor unless the homeowner is personally performing the work.
The 2026 fee schedule lists no City license fee for electrical contractors and says that fee is charged by the State.
If you are proposing work on a designated historic property, contact the City's Community Development Planner at DGraves@idahospringsco.com.

The Building Department page says the City adopted the 2024 building codes and the 2023 National Electrical Code, while the City's handout says the City enforces the 2018 edition of the International Building Codes. Ask SAFEbuilt which code edition applies to your project.
If Xcel Energy is your utility, the solar system cannot be sized by more than twice the annual kWh consumption of the site (Xcel's 200% Rule).

value.name: Building permit, valuation of work $1 to $500
value.notes: Higher valuations pay more under the schedule's valuation table.

permit_fees.notes: Fees are from the City of Idaho Springs Fee Schedule dated November 9, 2026 (Resolution No. 35, Series 2026). Building permit fees are based on valuation of work, and the schedule does not list a separate solar permit fee. The schedule lists a plan review fee of 65% of the permit fee, and the City's handout says City staff determine the plan review fee, which must be paid before review can start. The schedule lists a use tax of 3%. Card payments carry a $5.00 fee.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Income Qualified upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says customers who qualify under the terms of Income Qualified can receive an upfront rebate of $3 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer. Check that Xcel is your electric utility first.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Disproportionately Impacted Communities upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says Disproportionately Impacted Communities can receive an upfront rebate of $0.50 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer. Check that Xcel is your electric utility first.

rebates.notes: These are Xcel Energy programs. Xcel's page says that as of 10/05/2026 it moved $1,050,000 from Solar*Rewards C&I to the Solar*Rewards Residential IQ/DIC program. The City's Building Department page and 2026 fee schedule do not describe a City rebate for residential solar.
